summary: The root نسك (nsk) primarily means to devote oneself to religious exercises or devotion. It describes someone who becomes a devout worshipper, engaging in acts of piety.
lane: 5 تَنَسَّكَ ذ He devoted himself to religious exercises; applied himself to devotion; (S, Msb, K:) as also (S, K) and : (K:) or the last, he became a نَاسِك . (S.)

headwords.def: نَسَكَ He worshipped: used transitively. See an ex. in a verse of El-Aashà, in the S, art. نصب. See 5.
أَنْسَكَ [app. He washed and purified a garment]. (TA voce إِجْتَابَ.)
تَنَسَّكَ He devoted himself to religious exercises; applied himself to devotion; (S, Msb, K:) as also (S, K) and: (K:) or the last, he became a نَاسِك. (S.)
مَنَاسِكُ الحَجِّ The religious rites and ceremonies of the pilgrimage: or the places where those rites and ceremonies are performed. (Msb.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
